claims.claim: A human hair is roughly 80 micrometers (0.08 mm) wide
claims.definition: The average diameter of a human head hair is about 70-100 micrometers, with ~80 µm the commonly cited midpoint; fine blonde hairs run thinner, coarse dark hairs thicker. 80 µm = 0.08 mm.
claims.authoritative_source: Standard microscopy references (hair diameter ranges); e.g., 'Human hair diameter' compendia in microscopy texts
sources: Science Learning Hub: Hair and fibres
claims.notes: Narration uses the ~80 µm midpoint; the range is honest.

claims.claim: The unaided human eye resolves detail down to about 0.1 millimeters
claims.definition: Maximum visual acuity of the normal human eye at 25 cm near point corresponds to resolving features of roughly 0.1 mm (100 µm); anything smaller requires magnification.
claims.authoritative_source: Standard human-physiology/optics texts (visual acuity, minimum separable)

claims.claim: One continuous zoom runs hair width (~80 µm) to skin cell (~30 µm) to mitochondrion (~1 µm) to DNA width (~2 nm)
claims.definition: Typical mammalian skin cells (keratinocytes) measure ~25-40 µm across; a mitochondrion is ~0.5-1 µm wide and 1-2 µm long; the DNA double helix is ~2 nm wide. Ratios along the chain: hair→cell ~3×, cell→mitochondrion ~30×, mitochondrion→DNA width ~500×.
claims.authoritative_source: Alberts et al., 'Molecular Biology of the Cell' (cell and organelle size ranges); standard cell-biology size scales
sources: Alberts, Molecular Biology of the Cell
claims.notes: Narration cites the 30× cell→mitochondrion step and the 2 nm DNA width.

claims.claim: A mitochondrion about 1 micrometer wide burns sugar into ATP inside folded cristae membranes
claims.definition: Mitochondria (~0.5-1 µm wide) carry out oxidative phosphorylation: folded inner-membrane cristae host the electron-transport chain that converts sugar-derived carriers into ATP, the cell's energy currency.
claims.authoritative_source: Alberts et al., 'Molecular Biology of the Cell' (mitochondria chapter)
sources: Alberts, Molecular Biology of the Cell

claims.claim: The DNA in one human cell uncoils to about 2 meters, yet the double helix is only 2 nanometers wide
claims.definition: A human diploid cell carries ~6.4 billion base pairs; at ~0.34 nm per base pair along the helix, fully uncoiled DNA measures about 2 meters, while the double helix is ~2 nm in diameter — roughly 40,000× thinner than an 80 µm hair.
claims.measured_value: ~2 m uncoiled; ~2 nm helix width; 40,000× vs 80 µm hair
claims.authoritative_source: NCBI Bookshelf, 'The Machinery of Life'/molecular biology of the cell references; standard genome-length derivations
sources: Alberts, Molecular Biology of the Cell (DNA dimensions)

claims.claim: The human body contains roughly 30 trillion cells
claims.definition: Bianconi et al. (2013) estimate 3.72×10^13 cells (~37 trillion) in a reference adult male; ~30 trillion is the commonly cited order of magnitude across body sizes.
claims.authoritative_source: Bianconi et al., 'An estimation of the number of cells in the human body', Annals of Human Biology 2013
sources: Bianconi et al., Ann Hum Biol 40(6), 2013
claims.notes: Narration uses the common '30 trillion' order of magnitude.
